issue.subject: NOC Ticket Auto-Processing (NOC-AUTO)
issue.description:
**PRD:** https://rnd.frontiir.net/en/products/rt/requirements/noc-ticket-automation-prd (Wiki.js, published; Detail Reference: https://rnd.frontiir.net/en/products/rt/requirements/noc-ticket-automation-detail-reference)

Outcome: tickets assigned to the NOC queue are validated, enriched with CPE and network data, and either routed to the responsible team or remotely resolved automatically, with every decision recorded, so that MTTR drops. In the current context MTTR is measured for Remote Resolve tickets only. Target: under 5 minutes. No baseline can be measured (the current job runs every 2 hours). How MTTR is measured and who reports it is for the NOC Manager to define (outside Dev scope).

This Epic is proposed as the single structure for NOC-AUTO work, for team review. Scope, goals, constraints, risks and open questions are in the PRD.

Constraint (NFR, from SysOps/Infra): the automation must not add material load to RT and runs outside the RT framework. The boundary is the RT application plus its database (decided 2026-11-18); the load measure is not yet defined and is tracked by Task T1. SysOps/Infra's concerns on the rejected design (state machine tables in RT, database connection handling, indexing, workflow not decoupled from RT) are recorded in the PRD as addressed by the current asynchronous, decoupled design (2026-11-19). (Register AC51 is held here, not in a Story.)

**Background (reference only, not modified):** #21613 Product epic, #22265 Dev PRD draft, #21503 Node-RED API epic, #22497 Peppermint async BCS epic (cross-project, CPEMS). Old tickets are referenced as plain text only; no relations are created. #21573 (RT External API) is implementation context only.

## High-level workflow

{{mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant UI as RT Web UI
    participant API as RT External API
    participant NR as Node-RED
    participant WE as Workflow Engine
    participant K as Kafka
    participant RU as RTUtil
    participant PP as CPEMS Peppermint
    participant RT as RT REST2

    UI->>API: Ticket assigned to NOC queue, POST remote-resolve
    API->>API: Validate payload, eligibility, 24h duplicate check
    API-->>UI: 202 Accepted with run_id
    Note over API: Processing continues in the background
    API->>NR: Get CPE and network data by CPE ID (30s timeout, 3 attempts)
    NR-->>API: CPE, ONU, OLT, CA1, uplink data and flags
    API->>WE: Normalized data (Network Good, then Category Type)
    WE-->>API: Decision, Remote Resolve or Queue Transfer
    API->>K: Publish decision event (3 attempts)
    K->>RU: Decision event
    opt is_remote_resolved is true
        RU->>PP: Trigger async Best Channel Selection
        PP-->>API: Result webhook (sweeper polls if no webhook)
    end
    RU->>RT: Update ticket (queue, status, custom fields, comment)
    API->>API: Record Transaction Log for report and dashboard
}}

Diagram shows the high-level flow only. Failure paths (Manual Check, duplicate skip, failed publish) and the rules are in the PRD and Detail Reference.

children.subject: Design review with SysOps/Infra: automation runs outside RT, without material load on RT
Eligible tickets are picked up and every ticket is recorded
A ticket with a healthy network and no special category is remotely resolved
A ticket re-assigned within 24 hours is not processed twice
A ticket whose CPE data cannot be retrieved is flagged for Manual Check
OLT, PON and line-quality faults are routed to NOC with the findings
Fibre plant and ONU/CPE device faults are routed to the responsible team
Tickets with history, program or problem context are not auto-resolved
Tickets with tag, root-cause, new-customer or low-usage signals are routed to NOC
Every decision is delivered downstream and failed deliveries are kept
Remote Resolve triggers 2.4 GHz channel optimization (BCS)
NOC can review processed tickets in the Transaction Log UI and daily report
Confirm Node-RED (#21503) contract gaps with the owner
Agree design outputs: RT Web UI request schema, API route, Kafka topic, key and partition strategy
Record as-built implementation status per acceptance criterion
QA: derive Test Scenarios and Test Cases and the AC to Test Scenario to Test Case traceability
